module.purpose: Defines the typed records, validators, migrations, identifiers, and factory functions for comment threads, comments, and emoji reactions in tldraw.
module.summary: This module models optional, document-scoped comment collaboration records. It defines discriminated canvas anchors, thread resolution and soft-deletion state, comment messages, and independently stored emoji reactions. Validators enforce record shapes and bounded reaction identifiers, while retroactive migration guards prevent older schemas from receiving unsupported records. Factory functions create records and deterministic reaction IDs, and the exported configuration map enables coordinated client/server schema registration.
module.businessContext: Supports collaborative canvas discussions, anchored feedback, and reactions. Failure can prevent comments from syncing, corrupt anchor placement, or allow duplicate reactions and incompatible records.

boundaryConditions.intent: Rejects emoji strings longer than the maximum identifier-safe length.

errorHandling.action: Rejects emoji values outside the one-to-64-character range.

invariants.description: Every configured record has a fixed typeName matching its schema registration key.
New threads start unresolved, active, and with an empty metadata object by default.
New comments start unedited and active, preserving the supplied rich text body.
A reaction identifier deterministically represents the encoded comment, user, and emoji triple.
Comment messages are intended to be ordered by createdAt within their owning thread.

assumptions.description: Clients and servers must register the three comment record configurations identically.
Comment mutations are expected to use history ignore semantics rather than undoable history.
Sync infrastructure is expected to stamp or verify authorship and enforce soft-delete policies.

ambiguities.question: Which external schema registration path supplies commentSchemaRecords on clients and servers?
What concrete authorization layer enforces creator-only soft deletion and server-side identity stamping?

concurrencyModel.notes: Factories and validators are synchronous; deterministic reaction IDs allow concurrent clients or tabs to converge on one reaction record.
